newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee down in forwards on banker's statement.
newsitem.headline: India rupee down in forwards on banker's statement.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened against the forward dollar on Friday after a leading banker said that interest rates would go up in the long term, dealers said.

P.G. Kakodkar, chairman of India's largest commercial bank, the State Bank of India told a financial services conference on Thursday that India's domestic lending rates would go up in the long term because of massive demand for funds which could not be met through domestic sources.
July dollars were quoted 1.60/1.62 rupees in closing deals against the day's opening 1.52/1.55 rupees.
Dealers said the rupee had been under some pressure against the forward dollar on paying pressure in the last couple of days from banks rolling over swaps and also some import covering.
"But initially today, trade looked like being range-bound," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "In fact just before Kakodkar's statement was reported, sentiment had been slightly softish."
Sentiment changed on the report, he said.
He said several banks stepped into the forward market shortly thereafter and paying pressure pushed the rupee down.
In the spot market, the rupee appreciated to end Friday at 35.84/86 per dollar against the opening 35.87/88, dealers said.
"Supply remains good while demand is moderate," said a dealer. He said the rupee traded at a high of 35.8425 and a low of 35.88 on Friday.
Dealers said banks sold dollars to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at 35.85 rupees.
"The RBI was not in the market in the real sense of the word," said a dealer. "But it picked up dollars from a number of banks who went to it and offered them (dollars)."
